title: Setting material.diffuse_color does not affect the actual rendered Base Color on a node-based Principled BSDF material
problem: material.diffuse_color is a legacy/display property. When use_nodes=True (the default for materials created via bpy.data.materials.new()), the actual rendered appearance comes from the node graph -- specifically the Principled BSDF's 'Base Color' input socket -- which defaults to gray [0.8,0.8,0.8,1.0] and is NOT automatically synced from diffuse_color.
symptom: Code sets mat.diffuse_color = (r,g,b,1.0) and it appears to succeed (no error, the property reads back correctly), but the object renders/displays as flat default gray. Comparing bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value against mat.diffuse_color reveals they differ.

fix.summary: Set the BSDF node's Base Color input directly, not (or in addition to) diffuse_color.
bpy_bmesh_steps: bsdf = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
fix.code_snippet: verified directly on Bottle_Mat_v2, Flashlight_Mat_v2, SimpleBlock_Mat in runs/2026-08-07_decision-cycles/ (decisions 076-079)

evidence.note: found by comparing the two properties directly, not by visual inspection -- the bug was silent, no error, no warning

applicability: Any time a material's color needs to be set programmatically on a node-based material (use_nodes=True), verify the BSDF's actual input sockets, not just diffuse_color -- especially since assigning diffuse_color silently succeeds with no indication the render output is unaffected.
